description: Ability to review, test, and validate AI-generated summaries, classifications, and draft analytical content for accuracy, completeness, coherence, and fit for purpose.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Analytical material will increasingly be informed by AI-generated syntheses of stakeholder needs and option analyses. The position will need to assess whether those automated inputs are accurate, complete, and contextually appropriate before incorporating them into internal analysis or published materials.
justification: Current expectations emphasize participating in analysis and preparing material, but do not explicitly require evaluating AI-generated summaries or machine-assisted analytical outputs that will increasingly feed early-stage program analysis.

description: Ability to interpret AI-produced analytical material within the policy, program, respondent, and data-production context to determine relevance and appropriate use.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Analytical material will increasingly be informed by AI-generated syntheses of stakeholder needs and option analyses. The position will need to assess whether those automated inputs are accurate, complete, and contextually appropriate before incorporating them into internal analysis or published materials.
justification: The updated phase requires staff to focus less on manual drafting and more on contextual interpretation of automated outputs, which is not explicit in the current work-description.

description: Ability to assess whether trends or developments identified through automated tools are statistically, substantively, and operationally meaningful.
historic work: Key Activities - Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: Trend identification will increasingly include patterns emerging from AI-supported stakeholder feedback analysis and environmental scanning, not only from traditional statistical series. The role will need to distinguish meaningful developments from automated signal detection that may be spurious, biased, or weakly evidenced.
justification: The existing wording supports trend identification, but not the evaluation of trends surfaced through automated pattern recognition or feedback synthesis tools.

development area: Bias and representativeness in AI-supported needs analysis
description: Knowledge of common sources of algorithmic bias, coverage issues, and representativeness risks in automated consultation and feedback analysis.
historic work: Key Activities - Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: Trend identification will increasingly include patterns emerging from AI-supported stakeholder feedback analysis and environmental scanning, not only from traditional statistical series. The role will need to distinguish meaningful developments from automated signal detection that may be spurious, biased, or weakly evidenced.
justification: The role will need to recognize when AI-supported needs analysis may underrepresent certain stakeholders or overstate certain themes, a requirement absent from the current profile.

description: Ability to convert AI-synthesized stakeholder needs and option outputs into practical implications for survey methods, processes, and statistical products.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Recommendations for survey and program improvements will increasingly originate from AI-supported needs capture and option analysis. The role will need to validate those inputs, determine whether they reflect genuine user and stakeholder requirements, and help convert them into feasible methodological recommendations.
justification: Current expectations cover recommending improvements, but do not explicitly include translating AI-derived needs statements into methodologically feasible changes.

development area: Needs prioritization and option assessment in automated environments
description: Knowledge of how to evaluate user needs, trade-offs, risks, and feasibility when options have been pre-generated or pre-ranked by automated tools.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: Recommendations for survey and program improvements will increasingly originate from AI-supported needs capture and option analysis. The role will need to validate those inputs, determine whether they reflect genuine user and stakeholder requirements, and help convert them into feasible methodological recommendations.
justification: The updated process emphasizes strategic prioritization of needs over manual processing of inputs, creating a new expectation in assessing value, feasibility, and risk of suggested changes.

description: Ability to support users when requests, feedback, or needs statements have been captured or pre-processed by automated systems, including clarifying and correcting machine-interpreted content.
historic work: Key Activities - Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
change to work: User assistance will increasingly involve interpreting and clarifying outputs from automated intake or AI-assisted consultation processes. The role may support users whose requirements have been captured through automated channels by validating those requirements and resolving ambiguity or mismatch.
justification: Current user support expectations do not explicitly include handling AI-mediated interactions or correcting automated interpretations of user needs.

development area: Quality assurance of AI-generated review materials
description: Ability to evaluate AI-drafted briefs, needs summaries, and option analyses for subject-matter accuracy, internal consistency, and decision-usefulness.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.
change to work: Subject matter studies and reviews will increasingly incorporate AI-drafted background materials, synthesized needs assessments, and automated option summaries. The role will need to assess their reliability and provide subject-matter assurance before they are used by project teams or senior officers.
justification: The current role supports studies and reviews but does not explicitly require quality assurance over AI-generated supporting materials.

description: Ability to review automated requirements summaries, identify ambiguities or omissions, and refine them through stakeholder engagement into usable specifications.
historic work: Technical Activities - Communiction: Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Liaison work will shift from manually eliciting and consolidating requirements toward validating, refining, and translating requirements that have already been structured by AI or automated intake tools. The role will need to challenge machine-generated requirements where they miss context or misstate stakeholder needs.
justification: This activity already involves translating requirements, but the update adds a need to work from automated requirements outputs and detect where they require human correction.

description: Knowledge of the strengths, limitations, and governance considerations of AI-supported prioritization and planning outputs.
historic work: Technical Activities - Communiction: Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Liaison work will shift from manually eliciting and consolidating requirements toward validating, refining, and translating requirements that have already been structured by AI or automated intake tools. The role will need to challenge machine-generated requirements where they miss context or misstate stakeholder needs.
justification: Because automated tools may shape project priorities and target dates, the role needs stronger understanding of when automated prioritization should or should not be accepted.

description: Ability to revise AI-drafted explanatory material to ensure precision, conceptual integrity, readability, and alignment with official terminology.
historic work: Technical Activities - Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.
change to work: Writing and presentation work will increasingly involve reviewing, editing, and contextualizing AI-drafted content rather than producing all explanatory material manually. The role will need to ensure that automatically generated language accurately reflects official concepts and definitions.
justification: The current writing expectation does not explicitly cover critical review and correction of AI-generated wording of technical concepts.

description: Knowledge of how to describe, document, and maintain procedures involving AI and automation, including controls, review points, and user guidance.
historic work: Technical Activities - Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
change to work: Documentation may be partially auto-drafted, with the role contributing more through validation, adaptation, and ensuring operational relevance. Guidance materials may also need to explain new automated needs-identification processes and controls.
justification: The updated environment requires staff to maintain documentation about automated workflows and review AI-drafted procedural content, which exceeds the current manual-documentation emphasis.

development area: AI literacy for statistical business processes
description: Knowledge of how AI and automation are applied in needs specification, text synthesis, option analysis, and draft generation within statistical program work.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
change to work: The existing computerized-environment expectation broadens to include understanding how AI tools support needs identification, consultation analysis, and option generation. The role will require more specific literacy in AI-enabled analytical processes rather than general computerization alone.
justification: The current knowledge statement references a computerized environment broadly, but not AI-enabled workflow concepts now central to the updated phase.

description: Ability to use domain expertise to confirm, reject, or reframe emerging issues and needs identified through AI-supported analysis.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
change to work: This knowledge remains essential but must now be applied to evaluate whether AI-surfaced stakeholder needs and emerging issues align with genuine economic and social developments, rather than accepting automated categorizations at face value.
justification: The role already needs subject-matter awareness, but now must integrate it with validation of machine-generated issue detection and emerging-need categorization.

description: Knowledge of how to assess feasibility, risks, controls, and operational impacts when proposed statistical program changes depend on AI or automation.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Feasibility and impact assessment will now include consideration of automation-supported options and the implications of relying on AI-generated evidence or business case content. The role must understand both methodological feasibility and automation-related risks.
justification: Current feasibility assessment knowledge does not explicitly encompass AI-enabled options, automated evidence generation, or related quality risks.

description: Knowledge of methods for evaluating reliability, consistency, traceability, and appropriateness of AI-generated summaries, classifications, recommendations, and draft documents.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
change to work: Validation expectations expand beyond traditional computer outputs and database contents to include AI-generated summaries, recommendations, and draft materials used in needs specification. The role will need more explicit competence in validating non-deterministic outputs.
justification: The current statement supports assessing output from computer applications, but AI-generated text and recommendations create new validation demands beyond traditional deterministic outputs.

development area: Context-based challenge of automated needs outputs
description: Ability to use survey and respondent context to identify when automated needs summaries omit key populations, concepts, or operational considerations.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
change to work: This knowledge will increasingly be used to detect where automated needs capture misses nuances of the survey universe, stakeholder groups, or respondent impacts, and to ensure resulting recommendations remain appropriate.
justification: The role already needs survey-context knowledge, but it now must be applied to challenge incomplete or distorted machine-generated representations of needs across the survey universe.

description: Knowledge of how sponsor, participant, respondent, and user perspectives may be differently captured or weighted in AI-supported consultation and requirements processes.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.
change to work: Program context knowledge will also need to inform oversight of automated stakeholder-input processing, ensuring that sponsor, participant, and respondent perspectives are correctly represented and appropriately weighted.
justification: The current focus is on retrieval and processing of data, but the updated phase requires representation-sensitive oversight of automated needs processing.

development area: Governance of AI use within program mandates
description: Knowledge of how automated recommendations and draft outputs should be assessed against divisional objectives, governance expectations, and approved statistical practices.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.
change to work: This knowledge must now also support decisions about when automated needs-specification outputs align with divisional priorities and when human intervention is required to preserve policy, program, or methodological coherence.
justification: The modernized process introduces governance and alignment questions around automated recommendations not explicit in the current mandate-knowledge expectation.

development area: Evidence triangulation for AI-supported needs assessment

historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability
change to work: Internal data source knowledge may increasingly be used to verify or contextualize AI-identified needs and trends by comparing them against existing outputs and evidence rather than relying solely on automated summaries.
justification: The current expectation supports consistency checking, but future work will require more active triangulation between automated needs outputs and internal evidence sources.

development area: Privacy and policy compliance for AI-assisted work
description: Knowledge of legal, privacy, confidentiality, and organizational policy requirements governing the use of AI and automation in stakeholder engagement, needs analysis, and documentation.

change to work: Compliance knowledge must extend to the use of AI and automated tools in handling stakeholder inputs, needs documentation, and draft materials, including privacy, confidentiality, and acceptable-use considerations.
justification: The existing legal and policy knowledge focuses on data handling generally, but the updated phase requires understanding compliance implications of AI-assisted processing and drafting.

development area: Impact assessment of AI-enabled process changes
description: Ability to assess how AI and automation introduced into front-end statistical processes affect outputs, products, service quality, and subsequent methodological work.
historic work: Responsibilities - 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
change to work: Analysis of changes in computer technology will now more explicitly include assessing AI and automation introduced into needs specification and their effects on downstream outputs, service quality, and methodological decisions.
justification: The current responsibility references computer technology broadly, but the updated environment requires more explicit ability to analyze AI-driven process change and its downstream consequences.

development area: Conceptual risks in automated needs specification
description: Knowledge of how AI-driven categorization, summarization, and drafting can alter, narrow, or distort original stakeholder concepts and requirements.
historic work: Responsibilities - 6. Research and analysis: Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
change to work: This responsibility expands to evaluating how automated requirements capture, categorization, and drafting may impose constraints or distortions on the concepts and needs later reflected in program decisions.
justification: The role currently assesses constraints on data results, but now must also recognize conceptual constraints introduced earlier by automated interpretation processes.

description: Knowledge of alternative AI and automation approaches for consultation, needs intake, documentation, and related statistical process support, including their advantages and limitations.
historic work: Responsibilities - 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
change to work: The role will increasingly assess whether alternative systems should include automated and AI-enabled approaches to needs intake, consultation analysis, and documentation, while ensuring continued relevance and quality.
justification: This responsibility already includes proposing alternative systems, but future expectations require explicit familiarity with automation-enabled alternatives and their control requirements.

description: Ability to interpret, validate, and contextualize AI-generated summaries, signals, and prioritized information requests in support of statistical program analysis.

change to work: This activity expands to include analysis of AI-aggregated user requests, respondent feedback, environmental signals, and comparative benchmarking information. Analytical material will increasingly need to explain not just statistical findings, but also the rationale for accepting, rejecting, or prioritizing machine-identified needs.
justification: The current work-description emphasizes participation in analysis of program data, but does not explicitly require ability to assess AI-generated triggers, summaries, or prioritized needs. The updated process requires the employee to work with machine-supported evidence rather than only manually assembled inputs.

development area: Knowledge of automated data sourcing and output limitations

description: Understanding of the principles, sources, and outputs of AI-enabled monitoring of user demands, external developments, and peer-organization practices.

The role will shift from primarily identifying trends directly to validating whether AI-detected developments are substantively important, methodologically credible, and relevant to the program area.
justification: Effective validation requires understanding of how automated scanning tools identify patterns across user requests, feedback, and external practices. This is not explicit in the current work-description.

development area: Knowledge of end-to-end implications of automated needs identification
description: Understanding of how AI-supported needs assessment influences downstream survey design, operational procedures, respondent burden considerations, and statistical outputs.

Recommendations will increasingly be based on synthesized evidence from automated user-demand analysis, respondent feedback aggregation, and external benchmarking, requiring the employee to connect identified needs with implications for survey design and production methods.
justification: Because needs detection is increasingly automated, the employee must understand how early-phase automation can affect later methodological decisions and where human judgment is necessary.

development area: Communication of AI-supported findings to users

historic work: Key Activities - Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
change to work: User assistance will increasingly include clarifying how identified needs were prioritized and how user feedback may have been captured through automated channels. The role may need to help users interpret evolving requirements and communicate when AI-generated findings require human confirmation before action.
justification: The current activity focuses on providing data and assistance, but not on explaining AI-supported prioritization or the interpretation limits of automated findings to users.

description: Ability to assess completeness, relevance, and contextual appropriateness of AI-assembled materials used in subject matter studies and program reviews.

justification: The current work-description supports studies and reviews, but not the critical appraisal of machine-curated evidence packages that may frame those studies.

This shifts liaison from gathering inputs only through interpersonal channels to mediating between automated evidence and stakeholder judgment.
justification: The current liaison expectation does not explicitly require facilitation of discussions about AI-derived requirements or confidence in machine-supported recommendations.

development area: Plain-language explanation of automated analytical processes

change to work: Written and oral explanations will need to include AI-supported scanning methods, automated feedback synthesis, and benchmarking outputs in language accessible to non-technical audiences. This adds a requirement to explain both statistical and automated-process concepts clearly.
justification: The current communication requirement addresses technical/statistical concepts generally, but not AI-enabled analytical processes and their limitations.

development area: Knowledge of human-AI workflow documentation practices

change to work: Documentation will need updating to reflect automated monitoring procedures, interpretation protocols, escalation points for human review, and standards for using AI-supported needs assessment in program development and assessment.
justification: The current duty includes documentation, but future-state documentation must cover human-AI workflows, review controls, and responsible use procedures not currently specified.

change to work: This knowledge area remains central but is applied differently: staff must assess trends surfaced by AI systems and judge their relevance against real-world economic and social context. Subject-matter expertise becomes more important as a validation layer for automation.

development area: Knowledge of feasibility assessment using AI-supported evidence

change to work: Divisional mandate knowledge will be increasingly important for deciding which AI-detected needs should be acted on, deprioritized, or escalated. Automation may surface more candidate needs, but staff must filter these against mandate and policy constraints.
justification: The future process increases the volume and speed of incoming candidate needs; therefore mandate-based filtering and prioritization become more prominent than in the current description.

development area: Corroboration of automated findings using internal data sources
description: Ability to cross-check AI-generated needs assessments and trend signals against internal statistical outputs and metadata to verify consistency and relevance.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability
change to work: Internal data source knowledge will be used not only for traditional comparison and consistency checks, but also to validate or challenge needs detected by automated scanning and external benchmarking.
justification: The employee must increasingly use internal sources to corroborate machine-surfaced requests or emerging issues before methodological or program changes are proposed.

change to work: This responsibility expands to include assessing how AI-enabled needs identification changes workflows, products, service priorities, and evidence used in program planning. The role must examine whether automation improves responsiveness or introduces quality and governance risks.

development area: AI literacy in statistical concept development
description: Knowledge of how AI tools generate suggestions, their strengths and limitations, common error modes, and appropriate controls when using them for concept identification.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
change to work: The existing knowledge remains relevant but is no longer sufficient as stated. 'Computerized environment' now needs to encompass AI-enabled analytical environments where automated synthesis supports conceptual work. The role requires understanding both substantive theory and how AI tools may distort, simplify, or recombine concepts.
justification: The current bullet references a computerized environment generally, but the update specifically requires competency in AI-assisted conceptual work and the limits of automated synthesis.

description: Ability to translate new economic and social phenomena into measurable conceptual definitions and evaluate whether AI-assisted options capture those phenomena adequately.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of current and emerging economic and social issues relating to the program area in order to identify and assess trends and issues represented by statistical data series.
change to work: This knowledge now needs to be applied earlier in the process to assess whether AI-suggested concepts appropriately capture emerging issues from the user perspective. The role must judge whether suggested concepts are substantively meaningful, timely, and policy-relevant before they enter design.
justification: The update creates a stronger need to connect emerging substantive issues with concept framing rather than only later trend analysis.

description: Knowledge of criteria and methods for assessing whether a proposed concept can be operationalized reliably, efficiently, and consistently within statistical programs.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields: Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Feasibility assessment now begins earlier with concept options produced through AI-supported synthesis. The role must evaluate whether proposed concepts are measurable, coherent, and realistic for downstream program design.
justification: The update requires assessing feasibility not only of program changes generally, but of candidate concepts before formal specification.

description: Ability to test whether candidate concepts align with the survey universe, target population, reporting realities, and subject-matter boundaries.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
change to work: Subject and universe knowledge must now inform concept validation before method changes are even proposed. It becomes part of checking whether AI-suggested concepts actually match the target population, reporting units, and substantive reality of the survey domain.
justification: The role must now apply contextual knowledge to vet AI-assisted concept proposals at the concept-identification stage, not only to later method changes.

description: Knowledge of how sponsor priorities, respondent realities, and program constraints shape the final specification and certification of concepts.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.
change to work: This now includes understanding sponsor accountability and using program context to support concept specification and formal certification. The role must organize evidence and options in ways that fit sponsor decision-making and respondent realities.
justification: The update places explicit emphasis on sponsor accountability for final concept specification, which is only partially implied in the current contextual knowledge wording.

description: Knowledge of how to identify, assess, and compare internal and external documentary and data sources for use in AI-assisted concept development.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 5. Contextual knowledge: Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability
change to work: This element broadens from comparing related outputs to sourcing evidence for concept identification. Internal and external sources become inputs to AI-assisted synthesis, and the role must judge source suitability and comparability when constructing candidate concepts.
justification: The update explicitly includes use of internal and external sources in concept synthesis, expanding beyond current emphasis on internal data source comparison.

description: Ability to evaluate how AI and automation affect concept quality, workflow efficiency, methodological risk, and downstream statistical outputs.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
change to work: The reference to computer technology now explicitly extends to AI-enabled tools affecting concept identification and upstream design quality. Analysis must include how automation changes concept formulation quality, speed, risks, and documentation needs.
justification: The current wording is broad, but AI-enabled conceptual workflows require more specific evaluative capability around automated technologies and their quality effects.

description: Ability to assess the likely downstream effects of candidate concepts on collection, processing, comparability, interpretation, and data quality before they are formally adopted.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 6. Research and analysis: Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
change to work: This becomes a core upstream function. Instead of only assessing concepts after they influence results, the role must evaluate candidate concepts before downstream implementation, including the constraints introduced by AI-assisted concept generation.
justification: This existing bullet is highly relevant but requires a stronger preventive orientation focused on concept vetting before implementation.

description: Ability to map candidate concepts to implications for collection instruments, processing systems, metadata structures, outputs, and procedural changes.
historic work: Skills/Knowledge - 6. Research and analysis: Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
change to work: The role will need to connect concept choices generated in 1.4 with later procedural implications more explicitly. This means evaluating whether existing systems can support newly specified concepts and flagging required adaptations earlier.
justification: The update increases the need for early linkage between conceptual definition and operational system implications.

description: Ability to assess and compare existing holdings, administrative data, and alternative data against user requirements, including conceptual fit, timeliness, continuity, accessibility, metadata completeness, and statistical usability.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: This activity expands upstream from analysis of program data already in hand to analysis of candidate data sources and their metadata, including suitability, timeliness, continuity, restrictions on use, and alignment with user requirements. Analytical material will increasingly include source assessment summaries, option comparisons, and evidence supporting whether existing holdings or external data can satisfy requirements.
justification: The current wording emphasizes analysis of statistical program data, but the update requires systematic comparison of multiple candidate data sources before data are acquired or collection is designed.

description: Ability to produce auditable comparisons of data source options, decision rationales, and residual gap analyses in a systematic and reproducible manner.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: This activity expands upstream from analysis of program data already in hand to analysis of candidate data sources and their metadata, including suitability, timeliness, continuity, restrictions on use, and alignment with user requirements. Analytical material will increasingly include source assessment summaries, option comparisons, and evidence supporting whether existing holdings or external data can satisfy requirements.
justification: The update requires documented and rigorous assessment inputs to support sponsor certification that all relevant avenues were explored.

description: Knowledge of common administrative and alternative data types, their strengths, limitations, provenance issues, and implications for statistical use.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: This activity expands upstream from analysis of program data already in hand to analysis of candidate data sources and their metadata, including suitability, timeliness, continuity, restrictions on use, and alignment with user requirements. Analytical material will increasingly include source assessment summaries, option comparisons, and evidence supporting whether existing holdings or external data can satisfy requirements.
justification: The current role references validity of collected and processed data, but the future state requires stronger understanding of source metadata and acquisition constraints before data are used.

development area: Data market and source landscape awareness
description: Knowledge of evolving internal, administrative, and alternative data opportunities, including continuity risks, access conditions, and emerging source relevance to subject-matter needs.
historic work: Key Activities - Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: Trend identification will increasingly require awareness of developments in data availability, external data partnerships, and evolving administrative or alternative sources, not only trends in substantive statistical outputs. The role will help identify emerging source opportunities and risks affecting future statistical production.
justification: The update formalizes prioritization of existing and external data sources, so 'trends and developments' now include developments in the data supply landscape.

description: Knowledge of the formal sequencing and decision logic for prioritizing existing holdings, administrative data, alternative data, and only lastly new survey collection.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: This element is significantly affected because survey improvement can no longer be treated as a default response to unmet needs. Recommendations must now reflect the formal hierarchy: first existing holdings, then administrative/alternative data, and only then new survey options. Feedback will therefore include whether a survey should be reduced, redesigned, supplemented, or deferred based on source availability assessments.
justification: The current role supports survey-method improvements, but the update requires a first-principles assessment of whether surveys are necessary at all after exhausting existing and external sources.

description: Ability to evaluate trade-offs across collection modes and source types, including respondent burden, legal feasibility, operational complexity, and downstream integration impacts.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: This element is significantly affected because survey improvement can no longer be treated as a default response to unmet needs. Recommendations must now reflect the formal hierarchy: first existing holdings, then administrative/alternative data, and only then new survey options. Feedback will therefore include whether a survey should be reduced, redesigned, supplemented, or deferred based on source availability assessments.
justification: Recommendations will increasingly depend on comparing feasibility, quality, burden, and timeliness across source types rather than focusing mainly on survey methods.

description: Ability to explain data source options, limitations, legal or operational constraints, and quality implications clearly to users and stakeholders.
historic work: Key Activities - Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.
change to work: User support will increasingly include explaining source limitations, advising on data availability pathways, and clarifying whether needs can be met through existing or external sources rather than new collection. Assistance may also involve communicating source restrictions and quality caveats to internal users and partners.
justification: The updated process requires clearer communication about source suitability, restrictions, and why some requests may be met through specific existing or external data rather than surveys.

description: Ability to contribute to multidisciplinary assessments involving subject matter, methodology, operations, legal, privacy, and data acquisition stakeholders.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.
change to work: Subject matter studies and reviews will now more explicitly include source feasibility reviews, assessments of external data relevance, and evidence packages that support sponsor decisions and center-of-expertise collaboration.
justification: The role already supports studies and reviews, but future reviews must be more formalized and include legal, operational, and acquisition-related dimensions.

description: Ability to work effectively with centers of expertise, data custodians, and other functional specialists to articulate requirements, assess feasibility, and support source acquisition planning.
historic work: Technical Activities - Communiction - Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Liaison responsibilities expand to include collaboration with the center of expertise and possibly data holders or internal custodians of existing holdings. Translation of requirements now includes specifying source evaluation criteria, metadata needs, acquisition constraints, and priorities consistent with the mandated source hierarchy.
justification: The role currently liaises mainly with specialists and users, but the update requires more structured collaboration with acquisition specialists and possibly data suppliers.

description: Ability to translate subject-matter data needs into operational, metadata, quality, and delivery requirements that can inform legal or operational agreements.
historic work: Technical Activities - Communiction - Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.
change to work: Liaison responsibilities expand to include collaboration with the center of expertise and possibly data holders or internal custodians of existing holdings. Translation of requirements now includes specifying source evaluation criteria, metadata needs, acquisition constraints, and priorities consistent with the mandated source hierarchy.
justification: Negotiation-related support becomes more important where operational or procedural conditions affect access to external or administrative data.

description: Ability to communicate technical findings on source suitability, metadata, quality, and restrictions in plain language for decision-makers and collaborators.
historic work: Technical Activities - Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.
change to work: Written and oral communication will increasingly need to explain why certain sources are preferred, how suitability was assessed, and what legal, quality, or operational constraints apply. Documentation must be understandable across technical and non-technical collaborators.
justification: Future documentation must support rigorous, transparent source assessments across diverse audiences.

description: Ability to draft guidance, procedures, templates, and reports that standardize source discovery, suitability review, and gap-filling strategies.
historic work: Technical Activities - Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.
change to work: These outputs will need to incorporate source hierarchy rules, procedures for exhaustive source investigation, and monitoring approaches for suitability, continuity, and restrictions on use. Management reporting will likely include documented rationale for source choices and remaining gaps.
justification: The update requires more formal process documentation and monitoring around source exploration and suitability assessment.

description: Knowledge of how administrative and alternative data differ from survey data, including conceptual mismatch, coverage issues, quality limitations, and implications for estimation and interpretation.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Knowledge of statistical or economic theory and principles and the relevance of their application in a computerized environment, and the methods and techniques of data gathering, statistical estimation and economic modeling.
change to work: This knowledge area must broaden beyond traditional data gathering methods to include evaluation of repurposed data sources and their implications for statistical inference, quality, comparability, and fitness for use.
justification: Existing knowledge expectations are rooted in data gathering and modeling, but the update requires competence in assessing non-designed data sources for statistical purposes.

description: Knowledge of the operational, legal, technical, and quality factors that determine whether existing, administrative, or alternative sources can feasibly support a statistical program.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.
change to work: Feasibility assessment now explicitly includes whether new or modified programs should rely on existing or external sources before considering new surveys. The role will need to assess impacts of source choices across legal, operational, and quality dimensions.
justification: The current feasibility focus is on programs generally, while the updated process requires explicit evaluation of source-specific acquisition and usability conditions.

description: Ability to evaluate candidate sources before use, including provenance, conceptual fit, completeness, metadata adequacy, continuity, and risks to validity.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - Knowledge of the socio-economic concepts and methods to assess the validity of collected and processed data, the output from computer applications, the validity of database contents and results from alternative manipulations of data.
change to work: Assessment of validity expands to pre-acquisition and pre-use stages, requiring evaluation of conceptual alignment, provenance, source continuity, and whether source metadata support valid statistical interpretation.
justification: Current validity assessment is oriented to collected and processed data already in use; the update requires earlier assessment of candidate sources and their metadata.

description: Knowledge of how subject-matter concepts, definitions, and populations align or diverge across surveys, administrative systems, and alternative data sources.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of the subject and universe of the survey is required in order to propose suitable changes to statistical or reporting methods and techniques.
change to work: This becomes broader than survey universe knowledge alone; the role will need to understand how subject-matter concepts map imperfectly onto existing holdings and external administrative or alternative sources.
justification: The updated process deprioritizes new surveys, so conceptual mapping must extend beyond survey instruments to non-survey source structures.

description: Knowledge of responsibilities among subject matter sponsors, centers of expertise, legal/privacy functions, operational partners, and data suppliers in the data sourcing process.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.
change to work: The role will need a stronger understanding of sponsor accountability, center-of-expertise roles, and the broader network of data suppliers and custodians involved in securing and using data.
justification: The update introduces explicit sponsor accountability and center-of-expertise collaboration, altering who does what in source exploration and acquisition.

development area: Internal data holdings inventory and prioritization
description: Knowledge of how to systematically identify, document, compare, and prioritize existing internal data holdings against emerging user requirements.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of data sources within Statistics Canada in order to locate, analyze and compare related statistical output to ensure consistency and reliability
change to work: This element is directly expanded: internal data holdings must be exhaustively investigated and prioritized first. The role must therefore move from general awareness of internal sources to more systematic inventorying, comparison, and prioritization of internal holdings as the first-line sourcing option.
justification: This is a central update requirement and exceeds the current generic expectation to know internal data sources.

development area: Legal and policy constraints on source acquisition and use
description: Knowledge of how legislation, privacy requirements, data-sharing conditions, and operational agreements affect access, linkage, use, retention, and dissemination of existing, administrative, and alternative data.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge - Knowledge of the Statistics Act and other pertinent acts such as the Corporate Returns Act and Income Tax Act, and of Statistics Canada policies to ensure understanding and application in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of data. The position must have a particular awareness of the Statistics and Privacy Acts with respect to the security and confidentiality of data to ensure their own actions are in compliance.
change to work: Legal knowledge must be applied earlier and more actively in source assessment, not only during collection and processing. The role will need to recognize restrictions on use, sharing conditions, and possible legal framework implications when evaluating candidate sources.
justification: The update explicitly includes assessment and possible updates to the legal framework for data collection and use, so legal awareness must be more operationalized during source selection.

description: Ability to assess how source formats, metadata, transfer methods, storage needs, and processing requirements affect feasibility and downstream production.
historic work: Skills - 6. Research and analysis - Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.
change to work: Analysis must now include how changes in source access, delivery formats, metadata, and acquisition arrangements affect downstream outputs and service quality. Administrative services are no longer just a contextual factor; they are a potential data source and dependency.
justification: The updated process explicitly requires checking ICT resources, delivery arrangements, and source-related operational conditions.

description: Ability to compare conceptual, legal, operational, and quality constraints across multiple potential data sources and assess their implications for intended uses.
historic work: Skills - 6. Research and analysis - Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.
change to work: This element becomes more central and broader, requiring comparison of constraints across candidate sources before selection, including conditions of access, legal restrictions, source continuity, and definitional mismatch.
justification: The future task is not only to assess constraints on existing results but to compare prospective sources before they are adopted.

description: Ability to identify how adopting different source types requires changes to collection substitutes, integration processes, validation procedures, and analytical practices.
historic work: Skills - 6. Research and analysis - Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.
change to work: Analysis of alternative systems will now explicitly include alternative sourcing strategies and associated process redesign. Proposed changes may involve replacing or supplementing survey collection with internal, administrative, or alternative data and adjusting downstream methods accordingly.
justification: The update changes the meaning of 'alternative systems' from mainly procedural alternatives to source-strategy alternatives with broader operational consequences.

description: Ability to critically assess AI-generated analytical text, summaries, and recommendations against source evidence, methodological realities, and organizational context.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.'
change to work: This activity would expand from preparing analytical material manually to assisting with the validation and refinement of AI-generated analytical and business-case content. The role would need to check that automated summaries of current-state processes, proposed changes, and supporting evidence are accurate, complete, and appropriate for decision-making audiences.
justification: The current activity emphasizes participation in analysis and preparation, but the updated process requires review of machine-generated drafts for correctness, completeness, and suitability for governance decisions.

development area: Evidence traceability in automated analytical workflows
description: Knowledge of how to trace statements, options, and conclusions in AI-assisted drafts back to source analyses, program documentation, and operational inputs.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.'
change to work: This activity would expand from preparing analytical material manually to assisting with the validation and refinement of AI-generated analytical and business-case content. The role would need to check that automated summaries of current-state processes, proposed changes, and supporting evidence are accurate, complete, and appropriate for decision-making audiences.
justification: Business cases now require evidence assembled through automated means; staff must confirm how findings were derived and whether they remain defensible.

description: Ability to express survey and process improvement recommendations in terms of options, expected benefits, implementation considerations, risks, and resource implications.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.'
change to work: This activity becomes more explicitly tied to business-case option development. Feedback on methods and procedures will increasingly need to be framed in terms of costs, risks, feasibility, business impacts, and stakeholder implications as part of reviewing proposed 'To-Be' solutions generated with automation support.
justification: The current description focuses on methodological feedback, but the update requires translating such feedback into structured business-case recommendations and option assessments.

description: Knowledge of how collection, processing, editing, compilation, and dissemination constraints affect the practicality of proposed process changes.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.'
change to work: This activity becomes more explicitly tied to business-case option development. Feedback on methods and procedures will increasingly need to be framed in terms of costs, risks, feasibility, business impacts, and stakeholder implications as part of reviewing proposed 'To-Be' solutions generated with automation support.
justification: AI-generated proposals may present plausible but incomplete operational changes; the role must judge feasibility within survey and program realities.

description: Ability to explain, clarify, and defend data inputs and analytical conclusions used in automated business-case materials to internal and external stakeholders.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Provides data and assistance to users, within and outside Statistics Canada.'
change to work: Providing assistance would increasingly include supplying evidence, clarifications, and contextual information used to substantiate AI-assisted business-case drafts for sponsors, subject-matter specialists, or governance reviewers. The role may need to explain how analytical inputs support recommendations and resolve questions arising from automated summaries.
justification: Support to users now extends into supporting governance-ready documentation and answering questions on AI-assisted outputs.

development area: Critical review of automated option analysis
description: Ability to identify gaps, unsupported assumptions, inconsistent logic, and contextual inaccuracies in AI-generated option comparisons and impact statements.
historic work: Key Activities - 'Under guidance, participates in subject matter studies and reviews to support the work of project teams or senior officers.'
change to work: Subject matter review will increasingly include reviewing AI-generated descriptions of the current state, proposed future state, and associated impacts. The role will support project teams by identifying omissions, contextual errors, or weak assumptions in machine-drafted business-case sections.
justification: The updated process makes review of machine-generated material a routine part of supporting studies and project work.

development area: Requirements articulation for AI-enabled planning processes
description: Ability to communicate business, methodological, and program requirements in structured ways that support automated drafting tools and subsequent human review.
historic work: Technical Activities - Communication - 'Liaises with other subject matter specialists and users to develop and translate subject-matter requirements into specifications for system development, to suggest improvements to ongoing programs, to negotiate procedural modifications and to establish project plans, priorities and target dates.'
change to work: Liaison work would now include helping translate subject-matter and program requirements into inputs for AI-assisted business-case development and clarifying business requirements when automated drafts do not accurately capture operational needs. Communication becomes more iterative and quality-assurance focused.
justification: The role currently liaises on subject-matter requirements, but the update adds the need to communicate requirements and corrections within AI-enabled planning and approval workflows.

development area: Editorial refinement of AI-generated technical content
description: Ability to revise machine-generated technical and subject-matter language into clear, decision-ready wording appropriate for non-technical reviewers and approval bodies.
historic work: Technical Activities - 'Writes and presents detailed subject matter and technical concepts, definitions and terms in common terminology in order to explain and clarify divisional systems and applications.'
change to work: Writing responsibilities would shift from primarily authoring original explanatory content to also editing and refining AI-generated text so that business-case language is accessible, accurate, and aligned with organizational terminology and governance expectations.
justification: AI drafting increases the need for editorial control rather than only original composition.

development area: Quality assurance for automated management documentation
description: Ability to evaluate AI-assisted reports and planning documents for factual accuracy, internal consistency, audience suitability, and alignment with management information needs.
historic work: Technical Activities - 'Writes program information manuals, training packages, monitoring procedures and management reports for use by colleagues, operational staff and management in the development, implementation and assessment of statistical programs.'
change to work: Management reporting and program documentation would increasingly draw on automated first drafts. The role would need to review whether those drafts accurately reflect program processes, risks, and implementation considerations, especially where business-case components are reused in management reporting or planning documentation.
justification: The current writing expectation does not explicitly include validating machine-generated reports for governance and management use.

description: Knowledge of how automated systems generate program options, summaries, and assessments, and what types of methodological or operational errors commonly require human correction.
historic work: Skills - 4. Knowledge of specialized fields - 'Knowledge of methods, techniques, practices and procedures to conduct studies and to develop/assess the feasibility and impact of new or modified statistical programs.'
change to work: This knowledge remains central but must now be applied within AI-assisted option development and business-case review. Feasibility and impact assessment will need to include judging whether automated outputs have properly represented methodological dependencies, implementation assumptions, and operational realities.
justification: The role already requires feasibility and impact knowledge, but now must apply it to validating AI-generated proposals and assessments.

description: Knowledge of how sponsor priorities, stakeholder sensitivities, and organizational objectives should shape the interpretation and refinement of business-case options and recommendations.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge - 'Knowledge of program context, program sponsors, participants and respondents to plan and organize the retrieval and processing of data for research or development projects.'
change to work: Program context knowledge becomes more explicitly important for ensuring AI-generated business cases align with sponsor expectations, stakeholder impacts, and organizational priorities. The role would need to use contextual understanding to detect generic or misaligned recommendations in automated drafts.
justification: Automation can produce content that is structurally complete but insufficiently tailored to sponsor and stakeholder context.

description: Knowledge of how divisional mandates, program policies, and administrative procedures must be reflected in business-case narratives, option analyses, and recommendations.
historic work: Skills - 5. Contextual knowledge - 'Knowledge of the divisional mandate, objectives, programs, policies and activities to adhere to the various statistical and administrative practices and procedures involved in the collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation of statistical data.'
change to work: This knowledge would be applied more directly to governance-facing documentation. The role would need to assess whether AI-generated business-case sections properly align with divisional mandates, policy expectations, and administrative realities before submission.
justification: The current requirement supports operations, but the update extends its use into automated governance documentation review.

development area: Impacts of AI on statistical business process documentation
description: Knowledge of how AI-enabled drafting tools affect process documentation quality, review requirements, and the reliability of cost-benefit and risk narratives.
historic work: Skills - 6. Research and analysis - 'Analyzes changes in procedures, methodology, computer technology and administrative services to determine the effect on data output, products and services.'
change to work: Analysis now includes understanding the implications of automation and AI tools themselves on process design, documentation quality, and decision support. The role would need to assess not only program changes but also how technology-assisted drafting affects outputs and approval readiness.
justification: The existing analytical expectation includes computer technology broadly, but the updated process specifically introduces AI-enabled drafting and synthesis into core planning work.

development area: Detection of overstated confidence in automated outputs
description: Ability to identify where AI-generated narratives fail to reflect data limitations, definitional caveats, uncertainty, or operational constraints.
historic work: Skills - 6. Research and analysis - 'Assesses and determines the impact and the constraints on results of the different concepts, definitions and conditions under which the data was collected, processed and stored.'
change to work: This element would expand to include assessing the downstream effects of data limitations or definitional issues on AI-generated business-case conclusions. The role would need to ensure that automated drafts do not overstate certainty or omit caveats arising from data conditions.
justification: Automated drafting may suppress nuance unless a reviewer can identify where data constraints materially affect conclusions and recommendations.

development area: Structured option comparison for approval processes
description: Ability to compare current and proposed methods using criteria such as benefits, costs, risks, feasibility, resource needs, and stakeholder impact.
historic work: Skills - 6. Research and analysis - 'Analyzes current collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures to ascertain their relevancy and to propose changes or alternative systems.'
change to work: The role would still analyze current methods and alternatives, but proposed changes would more often be incorporated into AI-assisted business cases. This requires clearer comparison of 'As-Is' and 'To-Be' states and stronger assessment of alternatives in forms suitable for approval.
justification: The role already considers alternative systems, but the updated process requires presenting those alternatives in structured, decision-ready formats generated partly by automation.

description: Understanding how structured metadata, classifications, variable definitions, and design specifications are created, interpreted, and used across downstream statistical processes.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Preparation of analytical material will increasingly depend on design outputs that are standardized, machine-actionable, and metadata-rich. The role will need to use and interpret these design artefacts earlier in the production cycle, and provide informed feedback on whether automated and AI-supported design decisions preserve analytical utility, coherence, and publication readiness.
justification: The current work-description emphasizes analysis and preparation of material, but not the interpretation of machine-actionable metadata and structured design artefacts that now shape analytical products upstream.

development area: Analytical validation of automated design outputs
description: Ability to review AI-assisted or automated design outputs for coherence, usability, methodological integrity, and suitability for analytical production.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of statistical program data and assists in the preparation of analytical material for internal use and publication purposes.
change to work: Preparation of analytical material will increasingly depend on design outputs that are standardized, machine-actionable, and metadata-rich. The role will need to use and interpret these design artefacts earlier in the production cycle, and provide informed feedback on whether automated and AI-supported design decisions preserve analytical utility, coherence, and publication readiness.
justification: As analytical material increasingly derives from automated and standardized design processes, the role must judge whether those outputs remain fit for analytical and publication purposes.

description: Knowledge of how changes in variables, metadata structures, standards, and automated design choices affect time series continuity, comparability, and interpretation of trends.
historic work: Key Activities - Identifies statistical trends and developments.
change to work: Trend identification will be influenced by changes in variable design, metadata enrichment, interoperability standards, and automated methodological updates. The role must distinguish genuine substantive trends from apparent changes introduced by redesigned concepts, classifications, or digitally transformed data structures.
justification: The updated Design phase introduces automated and iterative redesign of variables and processes, which can affect comparability over time; the current description does not explicitly require this design-change awareness.

description: Knowledge of how outputs, variables, instruments, and operational processes are designed for automation, interoperability, reuse, and downstream integration.
historic work: Key Activities - Under guidance, participates in the analysis of data and suggests possible feedback on collection, processing, editing, compilation and presentation methods and procedures, and assists in the development of recommendations for improvements to survey methods and activities.
change to work: This is the most directly affected key activity. Feedback will increasingly concern digitally designed workflows, AI-assisted specifications, reusable standards, metadata structures, and interoperable output formats rather than only procedural or methodological adjustments in isolation. Recommendations will need to consider automation-readiness, standardization, and impacts across the end-to-end statistical process.
